notes:
Addressed all six findings from the review (1 medium, 5 low). Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Crypto && dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests` from D:\AI\Administration2 — build succeeded with 0 Warning(s)/0 Error(s) under TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, tests: 230 passed, 0 failed (224 prior baseline + 6 new facts, nothing regressed). No git command beyond read-only status was run; no file outside src/Wakeel.Crypto and tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests was touched.

FINDING 1 (medium — Content gating). Added `SetupDescription` (SetupContent.cs): FormatVersion, ExportedAt, ExportSeq, Org, Units, Office, Device, Employee, Includes — everything W03 needs to show, with DeviceSeed, OfficeKey and Revocation deliberately excluded. SetupPackage now carries the parsed SetupContent in a private `_content` field and exposes `Description` (always readable, built once in the constructor) and `Content` as `{ get { Checks.EnsureAcceptable(); return _content; } }`, so a refused file's device seed and office key are unreachable through Content exactly like every other entry, while the description remains available for a refusal screen. New test: The_device_seed_and_office_key_stay_out_of_reach_of_a_refused_file_while_its_description_does_not (an OtherDevice-refused package: package.Content throws, package.Description.Org/.Device/.Employee still read).

FINDING 2 (low — FirstRun landmine). Removed the parameterless `SetupExpectations.FirstRun` property; added `public static SetupExpectations FirstRun(string stagingDirectory) => new() { StagingDirectory = stagingDirectory }`. SetupPackageWriter's internal Verify() call (which never goes through Validate and never actually reads StagingDirectory) now builds `new SetupExpectations { StagingDirectory = "n/a" }` inline with a comment explaining why. Updated the five test call sites that referenced the old property: two now pass `new SetupExpectations()` (relying on the test harness's WithStaging helper to fill in the folder), one (the 'refuses to run without its own staging folder' test) now passes `new SetupExpectations()` directly and unmodified — exactly what it needs to prove the missing-staging refusal. New test: FirstRun_builds_expectations_that_carry_only_the_staging_folder, pinning the factory's shape.

FINDING 3 (low — unbounded/undeclared-tolerant logo preview). Added `SetupPackage.MaxLogoSize = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (A04's 2 MB logo cap). ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile now returns null when `_content.Includes.Logo` is false (never previews an entry the check list has already refused as Tampered), returns null when no logo.png entry exists, and throws CryptoException(Corrupt) when the manifest declares it larger than MaxLogoSize — all before any byte is decrypted. Two new tests: A_preview_is_null_when_the_description_never_declared_a_logo_even_though_one_is_present (logo present but includes.logo=false), A_logo_the_manifest_declares_larger_than_the_product_ever_writes_is_refused_by_the_preview (manifest edited to declare an oversized logo.png, re-signed with the org key so the container still opens).

FINDING 4 (low — device date inconsistency). SetupChecker.CheckDevice now translates a chain error of ErrorCode.Expired into ErrorCode.FutureDate on SetupCheckItem.Device, mirroring the translation Examine already applies to the root certificate (Revoked/BadSignature/Tampered still pass through unchanged). New test: A_device_certificate_dated_ahead_of_the_clock_is_a_future_dated_package_not_a_bad_device (device certificate issued 3 days ahead of the clock via a body `with` clause re-signed by the org key, everything else dated now; asserts SetupCheckItem.Device carries FutureDate).

FINDING 5 (low — cache threshold boundary). Changed SetupPackage.ExceedsCacheThreshold from `entry.Size > MaxCachedEntrySize` to `entry.Size >= MaxCachedEntrySize`, matching both the XML doc ('At or above it...') and the existing test's own name. Extended Small_entries_stay_cached_but_one_at_the_cache_threshold_or_larger_is_decrypted_again_each_time with a third entry sized exactly at MaxCachedEntrySize (via ReadGuide), asserting Assert.NotSame on two reads, alongside the existing small-cached and above-threshold-uncached cases.

FINDING 6 (low — undocumented partial writes on refusal). Documented on ContainerReader.ReadEntryTo, ContainerReader.ExtractTo and SetupPackage.ReadTo that on a CryptoException the destination has already received unverified bytes and the caller must discard them. ContainerReader.ExtractTo now wraps each entry's write in try/catch, deleting the just-written target file via a new best-effort TryDelete helper (swallows IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException, never masks the real exception) before rethrowing, so a refused container never leaves a half-written file in the installation folder; entries fully written before the failing one are left in place. New test: A_tampered_entry_leaves_no_partial_file_at_the_extraction_target (manifest understates logo.png's size and is re-signed so every check still holds; ExtractTo throws Tampered mid-copy and the test asserts the target file does not exist afterward).

Out of scope, left to the supervisor/B1 per the reviewer's own framing: the two missing_spec_items (package validity window; check-list arity/advisory-status projection) — both explicitly marked by the reviewer as decisions or interface work outside this package's nine-item spec, not defects in Wakeel.Crypto. Carried into open_issues.
